paper_id: Zhang et al. - 2015 - QA-share Towards efficient QoS-aware dispatching approach for urban taxi-sharing
title: QA-share: Towards Efficient QoS-Aware Dispatching Approach for Urban Taxi-sharing
motivation: Rush-hour taxis hard to hail while occupied taxis have seats; taxi-sharing can help but imbalanced design hurts passengers or drivers
problem_framing: Joint optimization of driver profit and passenger QoS under dynamic request arrivals, avoiding schedule oscillation
key_insight: Tip decay functions make profit and QoS objectives mathematically consistent—maximizing tips simultaneously maximizes passenger experience
method_signature: ILP + heuristic two-phase scheduling with map clustering, candidate taxi search, and weighted bipartite matching
evaluation_criteria: Profit increase over baseline, service rate of requests, oscillation percentage, processing window sensitivity
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: ILP only scales to ≤12 requests; oscillation still 3.2% at optimal threshold; travel time estimation could be more accurate
evidence_for_taste: without considering the Quality of Service
simply inserts the request to the end
only leads to a small number of requests
the execution time of Optimal-Share increases considerably
we did not notice much oscillation
thinking_moves: 把调度公平性问题 reframe 成两个正交目标的同时最大化
通过 tip decay function 把主观 QoS 量化为可优化函数
用 oscillation 阈值来工程化抑制动态调度副作用
先证 NP-hard 下界, 再设计可扩展启发式
